Let the vertical segment have endpoints

and the horizontal segment have endpoints
\[
C=(1,1),\quad D=(3,1).
\]

A rotation center must be equidistant from each endpoint and its image. There are only two possible endpoint pairings:

1. \(A\mapsto C,\ B\mapsto D\).  
   The perpendicular bisectors of \(AC\) and \(BD\) meet at
   \[
   (1,3)=W.
   \]
   So \(W\) works.

2. \(A\mapsto D,\ B\mapsto C\).  
   The perpendicular bisectors of \(AD\) and \(BC\) meet at
   \[
   (0,0)=U.
   \]
   So \(U\) works.

Checking \(T\) and \(V\) gives mismatched distances to the endpoints, so neither can be the center. Hence the possible centers are exactly \(U\) and \(W\).
